summary: My work experience sits at the intersection of two things that don't often meet: the boardroom where mining strategy gets decided, and the underground sites where it actually plays out.At McKinsey & Company, I led transformation workstreams for global and Indian mining companies. The core of that work was structured problem-solving — taking a vague, high-level performance gap and breaking it down into a clear, testable diagnosis — combined with stakeholder management, since client teams rarely agreed upfront on what "broken" actually meant. Getting alignment on the diagnosis was often harder than designing the fix.Before that, at MOIL Limited, I managed production planning, safety, and environmental programs across underground mine sites — driving horizontal development to record levels and rebuilding safety protocols from the ground up. That role forced me to own real trade-offs: output targets against safety margins, compliance timelines against what a site could realistically absorb. Decisions there had immediate, physical consequences, which shaped how I think about risk — not as an abstraction, but as something with a direct cost if you get it wrong.The two experiences compound each other. When I evaluated a strategy recommendation at McKinsey, I wasn't just checking whether the logic held — I was checking whether it would survive contact with an actual mine site, because I'd been on that side of the table. That's the skill I'd point to as most transferable: rigorous diagnosis, disciplined risk-weighing, and a bias toward solutions built to hold up in practice, not just on paper.At ISB, I'm sharpening that same combination — building out the analytical and strategic toolkit while keeping the operator's instinct for what actually works

job_description: As a Chief Manager (Mining) at Coal India Limited, I was responsible for overseeing the operations of three coal mining projects: Jharkhand Mining Project, Tapin North, and Tapin South. This role involved comprehensive management of all mining activities, ensuring production efficiency, safety, and compliance with regulations. Additionally, during the COVID-19 lockdown, I implemented specific strategies to manage coal production while adhering to safety protocols and maintaining operational continuity. Implementation of Health and Safety Protocols: Developed and enforced strict health and safety protocols to protect workers from COVID-19. Implemented social distancing measures, provided personal protective equipment (PPE), and conducted regular health screenings. Operational Continuity Planning: Developed contingency plans to ensure operational continuity despite workforce reductions and supply chain disruptions. Implemented staggered shifts and remote working arrangements where possible to minimize contact and maintain productivity. Use of Technology and Remote Monitoring: Leveraged technology for remote monitoring and management of mining operations to reduce the need for on-site personnel. Utilized real-time data analytics and remote communication tools to oversee operations and make data-driven decisions. Supply Chain Management: Coordinated with suppliers to ensure the continuous supply of essential materials and equipment despite logistical challenges. Implemented strategies to mitigate the impact of supply chain disruptions on production schedules. Employee Support and Communication: Maintained open lines of communication with employees to provide updates, support, and address concerns related to COVID-19. Offered mental health support and resources to help employees cope with the stress and uncertainty of the pandemic.
summary: With a robust educational foundation in mining engineering from ISM Dhanbad, graduating in 1987, I embarked on my professional journey with Coal India Limited. Over the past 38 years, I have cultivated a profound and diverse expertise in both underground and open-cast mining operations, navigating through various capacities and roles within the organization.. In the initial 16 years of my tenure, I honed my skills in underground semi-mechanized mining operations. This period involved intensive work in developing and managing mining systems that optimized safety and productivity. I led efforts in implementing advanced mining techniques, including room and pillar mining, longwall mining, and the use of continuous miners and shuttle cars, ensuring efficient coal extraction and minimal environmental impact. My role extended to overseeing ventilation systems, ground control measures, and the application of cutting-edge technology to enhance the safety and efficiency of mining operations. Transitioning to open-cast mechanized mining for the subsequent 17 years, I embraced the challenges of large-scale surface mining projects. Here, I specialized in deploying high-capacity earth-moving machinery such as draglines, shovels, dumpers, and surface miners. My technical acumen facilitated the adoption of modern technologies like GPS-based fleet management systems, automated drilling and blasting techniques, and real-time monitoring systems to optimize production and reduce operational costs. I played a pivotal role in the implementation of highwall mining systems and in-situ gasification projects, pushing the boundaries of coal extraction methodologies. I have been instrumental in spearheading projects that emphasize sustainable mining practices. I have championed the integration of environmentally friendly technologies, such as reclamation planning, water management systems, and the use of renewable energy sources within mining operations. My commitment to safety is unwavering, having developed and enforced rigorous safety protocols, emergency response plans, and training programs aimed at minimizing occupational hazards and ensuring the well-being of the workforce. I have a proven track record in leadership and project management. I have led multidisciplinary teams through complex projects, fostering a culture of innovation, collaboration, and continuous improvement. My strategic vision and operational insights have contributed to significant enhancements in productivity, cost-efficiency, and compliance with regulatory standards.

company_description: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is the space agency of the Government of India headquartered in the city of Bengaluru. Our vision is to "harness space technology for national development", while pursuing space science research and planetary exploration. ISRO is managed by the Department of Space (DoS) of the Government of India. Indian Space Research Organisation, formed in 1969, superseded the erstwhile INCOSPAR. ISRO is one of the six largest space agencies in the world. ISRO maintains one of the largest fleet of communication satellites (INSAT) and remote sensing (IRS) satellites, that cater to the ever growing demand for fast and reliable communication and earth observation respectively. ISRO develops and delivers application specific satellite products and tools to the Nation: broadcasts, communications, weather forecasts, disaster management tools, Geographic Information Systems, cartography, navigation, telemedicine, dedicated distance education satellites being some of them. The PSLV was developed as a cost efficient and reliable launch system which went on to become a favoured carrier for satellites of various countries due to its reliability and cost efficiency, promoting unprecedented international collaboration. The Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV) was developed keeping in mind the heavier and more demanding Geosynchronous communication satellites. Future readiness is the key to maintaining an edge in technology and ISRO endeavours to optimise and enhance its technologies as the needs and ambitions of the country evolve. Thus, ISRO is moving forward with the development of heavy lift launchers, human spaceflight projects, reusable launch vehicles, semi-cryogenic engines, single and two stage to orbit (SSTO and TSTO) vehicles, development and use of composite materials for space applications etc.

company_description: The National Institute of Disaster Management (NIDM) was constituted under an Act of Parliament with a vision to play the role of a premier institute for capacity development in India and the region. The Institute believes that disaster risk reduction is possible only through promotion of a "Culture of Prevention" involving all stakeholders. NIDM is proud to have a multi-disciplinary core team of professionals working in various aspects of disaster management. In its endeavor to facilitate training and capacity development, the Institute has state-of-the-art facilities like class rooms, seminar hall and video-conferencing facilities etc. The Institute has a well-stocked library exclusively on the theme of disaster management and mitigation. The Institute provides training in face-to-face, on-line and self-learning mode as well as satellite based training. In-house and off-campus face-to-face training to the officials of the state governments is provided free of charge including modest boarding and lodging facilities. NIDM provides Capacity Building support to various National and State level agencies in the field of Disaster Management & Disaster Risk Reduction. The Institute's vision is to create a Disaster Resilient India by building the capacity at all levels for disaster prevention and preparedness.

summary: PISQRE LEARNING was born out of a real and recurring problem we observed in the education ecosystem. Over the years, we noticed that many students struggle to truly understand the concepts taught in colleges and institutions. While professors and doctors are highly knowledgeable, they often have limited time to address individual doubts. As a result, students are left with unresolved questions gaps that teaching assistants (TAs) are also sometimes unable to bridge. We repeatedly saw students reaching the final stages of their academic journey with the pressure to score well in exams, yet lacking conceptual clarity. Despite hours of studying, the absence of strong fundamentals often affected both their confidence and performance. One night, around 1:00 AM, reflecting on these challenges and the repeated concerns shared by students, the idea of building a better learning platform took shape a platform designed specifically to connect students with tutors who prioritize concepts, clarity, and understanding over shortcuts. We consistently encountered learners expressing similar concerns that some tutors could solve problems but could not explain the underlying concepts clearly. This reinforced our belief that knowing answers is not the same as understanding concepts.That realization became the foundation of PISQRE LEARNING. Our approach is simple yet strict: conceptual clarity comes first. Tutors are evaluated for their depth of understanding before engaging with students, ensuring that learning is meaningful, structured, and future-ready. Today, PISQRE LEARNING stands as a platform built on real experiences, real student challenges, and a commitment to restoring depth, clarity, and trust in education.

summary: Mechanical engineer with nine years in oil and gas, eight of them at ONGC across offshore operations and, currently, machinery procurement and projects.I spent over five years offshore on a process complex in the Western Offshore Basin, working hands-on with the machines that keep production running — gas turbines driving process gas compressors and turbo generators, centrifugal and water injection pumps, screw compressors, and the diesel engines behind fire water and emergency power. Maintenance, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, commissioning, and mechanical scopes through shutdowns, all under permit on live installations. It now runs across 66 wells.Six Sigma Black Belt. B.Tech in Mechanical Engineering from IIT (ISM) Dhanbad. Earlier at ISRO on cryogenic propulsion and Tata Motors in engine production.What interests me most is where machinery knowledge meets data — using what a machine is already telling you to act before it fails, rather than after.

Instead of giving up, I decided to understand marketing from the ground up. That journey led me to pivot at Bitsphere Infosystem, where my team and I now help businesses generate predictable growth through digital marketing. Today, we work with startups, SMEs, and established brands, running Meta and Google Ads campaigns to generate qualified leads and improve conversions. We've also had the opportunity to work with brands such as Hero, Hyundai, and several regional and corporate businesses. As we worked with more businesses, we noticed a common challenge. Many small and medium-sized businesses couldn't afford to rely solely on paid advertising. At the same time, they were missing out on customers searching for them on Google and increasingly through AI-powered search experiences. That's why we built Revplies. Revplies helps businesses strengthen their Google Business Profile by improving reviews, reputation, profile optimization, and customer engagement, making them more visible on Google and increasing their chances of being recommended by AI platforms. While solving one problem, we discovered another. Businesses were sending more messages than ever, yet customer engagement was declining. Traditional messaging channels had become crowded, making it difficult to capture attention and nurture leads effectively. To address this, my team and I built WhatsRCS- a platform that enables businesses to use RCS Business Messaging for richer customer conversations, better lead nurturing, and higher engagement. summary: I'm an AI/ML Engineer and M.Tech researcher at IIT Tirupati (IIT ISM Dhanbad alumnus), working at the intersection of generative modelling, financial ML, and production-ready AI systems. My current focus: making generative models actually useful, not just visually convincing. Recent work that defines how I think: Trained Diffusion Models and TimeGAN on financial time series to generate synthetic stock data. Diffusion looked perfect. TimeGAN won on predictive performance. That gap between visual realism and temporal logic is now the core question driving my research. Building RAG systems that go beyond basic retrieval, exploring chunking strategies, embedding choices, vector search, and evaluation frameworks to make LLM applications genuinely reliable in production. Built Finsphere, a React Native fintech application integrating mobile banking, microfinance, and digital insurance, because good AI needs good infrastructure around it.What I care about: Most people in this space optimise for what looks impressive. I optimise for what actually works when tested on real data, real users, and real constraints. That means being honest when a model fails. Building systems end-to-end. And asking better questions before writing a single line of code.What I'm exploring next: Hybrid generative architectures that combine Diffusion's global smoothness with TimeGAN's temporal coherence, and whether that unlocks better synthetic data for downstream forecasting.If you're working on a problem where AI needs to be reliable, not just impressive, I'd like to hear about it. DM me or connect here.

I work on natural hazards on the gap between a map predicting where risk falls and a measurement of whether it actually does. Most of my research has stayed in one place. Since my M.Sc. dissertation, I've been studying landslides in the Sikkim Himalaya, and my M.Tech thesis at IIT (ISM) Dhanbad returned to that terrain with a harder toolkit: comparing classical, ensemble, and deep-learning susceptibility models against one another, then testing their predictions against PSInSAR displacement time series from Sentinel-1. A susceptibility map is a static claim about a landscape that isn't static. Closing that gap is what interests me because it's what must happen before a hazard map can warn anyone. Before the M.Tech I spent two and a half years as a GIS Analyst with the Government of West Bengal, working on watershed development under PMKSY-WDC 2.0. The maps I made there went to administrators deciding where to spend money, not to journals. That changed what I think a model is for. I also work on the human side of spatial analysis. With colleagues in Midnapore, I co-authored a Springer book on using GIS to improve health outcomes in urban slums, and I continue to publish on healthcare access, urban heat, land-use change, and groundwater potential. Alongside my research, I teach GATE Geomatics Engineering through GeoAcademy, using the same syllabus I sat for in 2024. Students I've taught have gone on to IIT (ISM) Dhanbad, IIT Jodhpur, and IIEST Shibpur. I review for Scientific Reports, GeoJournal, Discover Environment, and Discover Public Health. Tools: Python, Google Earth Engine, SNAP, MintPy, SARPROZ, ArcGIS, QGIS. Currently seeking PhD positions in natural hazards modeling and early warning systems.

company_description: Ispat Industries Limited (IIL) is one of the leading integrated steel makers and the largest private sector producer of hot rolled coils in India. Set up as Nippon Denro Ispat Limited in May 1984 by founding chairman Mr M L Mittal, IIL has steadily grown into a Rs 9,400-crore company, assuming its position as flagship of the reputed Ispat Group. A corporate powerhouse with operations in iron, steel, mining, energy and infrastructure, the Group today figures among the top 20 business houses in the country. Headquartered at Mumbai, IIL employs a total of 3000 people and is the leader in the national speciality steel market. The company's core competency is the production of high quality steel, for which it employs cutting edge technologies and stringent quality standards. It produces world-class sponge iron, galvanized sheets and cold rolled coils, in addition to hot rolled coils, through its two state-of-the art integrated steel plants, located at Dolvi and Kalmeshwar in the state of Maharashtra. The sprawling 1,200 acres Dolvi complex houses the 3 million tonne per annum hot rolled coils plant, that combines the latest technologies - the Conarc process for steel making and the compact strip process (CSP) - introduced for the first time in Asia. The complex also has a 1.6 million tonne per annum sponge iron (DRI) plant, which was commissioned in 1994 as the world's largest and most efficient gas-based single mega module plant. Moreover, the Dolvi complex is home to a 2 million tonne blast furnace and also boasts a mechanised multi-functional jetty situated nearby, that facilitates the automation of raw material handling. A new 2.24 million tonnes per annum sinter plant, a 1260 tonnes per day oxygen and a new electric arc furnace have also been commissioned at IIL Dolvi.

Only 2–3% make it. Sixteen-year-old me listened, paused, and said: “I want to be that 3%.” If I could go back in time, I’d hug that kid and thank her for teaching me how to fight for what I truly want. From Supply Chain & Operations at AB InBev, to Growth & Strategy roles at early-stage startups like 10X and PandaMoney, to Product exposure at Hyperpure (Zomato), and marketplace and growth work with Weekday (YC-backed). I’ve tried my hand at business analytics, growth strategy, operations, product thinking, and technical problem-solving, learning that real growth often comes from stepping outside comfort zones. Sometimes confidently, sometimes nervously, and sometimes with a very messy VS Code terminal. What ties all of this together is my interest in business growth, strategy, and operations, backed by analytical thinking and hands-on execution. I enjoy working at the intersection of data, people, and systems, especially in fast-moving, ambiguous environments. Beyond work, I value good conversations. The kind that aren’t just logical, but warm. I love listening to stories, understanding people, exchanging perspectives, and being in spaces that leave you thinking a little deeper or smiling a little wider. Sometimes growth comes from action; sometimes it comes from stillness. And as Krishna says in the Bhagavad Gita, “A man is made by his belief. As he believes, so he is.” So, believe. Things have a way of working out, often better than we imagined. Still learning. Still growing. Still trusting the process. One day at a time.

company_description: MOIL is a Schedule “A” Miniratna Category-I Company. It was originally incorporated as Manganese Ore (India) Limited in the year 1962. This product is used for the manufacture of dry battery cells. EMD produced by the Company is of good quality and well accepted by the market. A Ferro manganese plant having a capacity of 10,000 MT per annum was also set up in 1998 by MOIL for value addition. Oil India Limited which was accorded "MAHARATNA" status on 04th August, 2023, is a state-owned enterprise of the Government of India, under the administrative control of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas and is the second largest national oil and gas company in India. In 1961, it became a joint venture company of Government of India and Burmah Oil Company Limited, UK. In 1981, OIL became a wholly owned Government of India enterprise. In FY 2022-23, OIL achieved highest ever Revenue & Profit after Tax (PAT) and also achieved highest ever Natural Gas production during the year. In 2021, OIL acquired additional 54.16% ownership interest in Numaligarh Reìnery Limited (NRL) making OIL the promoter & holding company of NRL. OIL has carved a niche as a leading oil and gas company in the upstream sector with a legacy of hydrocarbon exploration for over six decades and having a share of around 9% of the country’s total crude oil and natural gas production. The company has significant presence across the entire value chain in the hydrocarbon sector, it also produces Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) and transports crude oil and refined petroleum products through cross-country pipelines. The company’s In-Country operations are spread over the areas in the states of Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram, Tripura, Nagaland, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh and Rajasthan and offshore areas in Andaman, Kerala-Konkan and KG shallow waters. The company operates a 1157 Km long crude oil pipeline in the Northeast for transportation of crude oil produced by both OIL and ONGCL in the region to feed refineries.

company_description: About Patna Metro Rail Project Patna Metro Rail, spearheaded by Patna Metro Rail Corporation Ltd (PMRCL), is revolutionizing urban transit in Bihar’s capital through a modern Mass Rapid Transit System (MRTS). Phase-1 comprises two strategic corridors: Red Line (East–West Corridor): ~16.86 km, with 14 stations—9.36 km elevated and 7.5 km underground—connecting Danapur Cantonment and Khemnichak. Blue Line (North–South Corridor): ~14.56 km, with 12 stations. The 6.1 km priority stretch (Malahi Pakri to New ISBT) is set to inaugurate in August 2025, with full corridor operations expected by 2027–28. The project is being developed with a robust financial model (20% each from state and center, 60% JICA loan), at an estimated cost of ₹13,400–13,900 crore. Technical specifications include a broad-gauge track system, 25 kV AC overhead electrification, and CBTC signaling, enabling top speeds of 80 km/h and a projected daily ridership of 210,000 commuters. Key players involved: RITES (DPR), DMRC & Egis JV (consultancy), L&T, HCC, YFC–MCL, NCC, Quality Buildcon, KEC, Otis, Johnson Lifts, among others. The priority Blue Line stretch is nearing operational readiness, supported by modern depots, control systems, and passenger-centric station amenities including escalators, lifts, commercial spaces, and enhanced safety measures. ⚠ Disclaimer: This is not an official page of the Patna Metro Rail Project; it is an independent informational and community-driven overview. All information shared is based on publicly available sources and intended to promote awareness about the railway sector. For official updates, please refer to the official website of Patna Metro https://pmrconline.in/

EMIL envisions a future powered by green and clean energy. At present, we have a combined portfolio of 155 MW of solar and wind power. company_description: Oil India Limited (OIL) is a fully integrated Exploration & Production company in the upstream sector, with origin dating back to the glorious year (1889) of oil discovery in India. Oil India Limited which was accorded "MAHARATNA" status on 04th August, 2023, is a state-owned enterprise of the Government of India, under the administrative control of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas and is the second largest national oil and gas company in India. Oil India Private Limited was incorporated on 18th February 1959, to expand and develop the newly discovered oil fields of Naharkatiya and Moran in the North-Eastern region of India. In 1961, it became a joint venture company of Government of India and Burmah Oil Company Limited, UK. In 1981, OIL became a wholly owned Government of India enterprise. In FY 2022-23, OIL achieved highest ever Revenue & Profit after Tax (PAT) and also achieved highest ever Natural Gas production during the year. In 2021, OIL acquired additional 54.16% ownership interest in Numaligarh Reìnery Limited (NRL) making OIL the promoter & holding company of NRL. OIL has carved a niche as a leading oil and gas company in the upstream sector with a legacy of hydrocarbon exploration for over six decades and having a share of around 9% of the country’s total crude oil and natural gas production. The company has significant presence across the entire value chain in the hydrocarbon sector, it also produces Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) and transports crude oil and refined petroleum products through cross-country pipelines. The company’s In-Country operations are spread over the areas in the states of Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram, Tripura, Nagaland, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh and Rajasthan and offshore areas in Andaman, Kerala-Konkan and KG shallow waters. The company operates a 1157 Km long crude oil pipeline in the Northeast for transportation of crude oil produced by both OIL and ONGCL in the region to feed refineries.
